text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Hydrographer PHILLIP PARKER KING was born on Norfolk Island in 1791. He charted waters round Australia and South America and later settled in Australia.

Australian geologist and photographer RICHARD DAINTREE, who opened up several Queensland goldfields, was born in 1832. He became Queensland's Agent-General in London and had the DAINTREE Rainforest named after him.

Australian Bohemian writer DULCIE DEAMER was born in 1890. She was a fixture in pre-war Kings Cross in her leopardskin and reportedly "enlivened many a party by doing the splits and dancing the hula-hula".
Swedish/Australian cartoonist NILS JOHNSON, who gave us the comic strip "Uncle Joe's Horse, Radish", was born in 1890.
South African novelist Sir LAURENS VAN DER POST, whose books include "The Lost World of the Kalahari", was born in 1906. He was a travel writer and a conservationist.

American actor and comedian DICK VAN DYKE, who was best known for the television series "The DICK VAN DYKE Show", was born in 1925. He also appeared in the film "Mary Poppins" with JULIE ANDREWS. His career is still going strong, with a TV series as a crime-fighting medic.
Canadian stage and screen actor CHRISTOPHER PLUMMER, whose films include "Waterloo", "The Sound of Music" and "The Fall of the Roman Empire", was born in 1929.

American guitarist with the 'Doobie Brothers' JEFF 'SKUNK BAXTER, was born in 1948. He was with the band from 1974 to 1978 and then became a studio musician and producer. He was on records by STEELY DAN, JONI MITCHELL, CARLY SIMON, LITTLE FEAT and ROD STEWART.
** EVENTS **
1577 : Sir FRANCIS DRAKE set off on his round-the-world
voyage.
1862 : Confederate General ROBERT E. LEE inflicted a body

blow to the Union Army at Fredericksburg. Union general AMBROSE BURNSIDE planned to sweep LEE aside and push on to Richmond. His plan went astray and the federal forces were repulsed each time they attacked and suffered the loss of 12,500 men. Richmond remained in Confederate hands.
1867 : Irish bombers blew up the outer wall of London's
Clerkenwell prison in a bid to rescue a jailed inmate. The blast demolished the wall and several nearby houses and killed 12 people and injured more than 100 locals. But the jailed Irishman

remained behind bars. Police said the bombers were Fenians, members of the Irish Republican Brotherhood, which was founded 10 years earlier with the assistance of Irish Americans. Their aim was to overthrow British rule in Ireland and had mounted several attacks on British property.
1903 : The ice-cream cone was born in the United States.

Ice-cream was a Chinese invention and explorer MARCO POLO took the formula back to Italy in 1295. Americans had been eating the ice confectionery since the 1850s when Baltimore milk dealer JACOB FUSSELL built a factory. New York ice-cream merchant ITALO

MARCIONE patented the perfect container for the ice-cream - the cone. It was easy to hold, no spoon was needed and when the ice cream was finished the cone could be eaten. America's avid ice-cream eaters wasted no time in taking to the ice-cream cone.
1904 : The first electric train came into service on
London's Metropolitan Railway.
1907 : The liner "Mauretania" ran aground at Liverpool.
1911 : The P&O liner "Delhi" foundered with the Princess
Royal on board but she and most of the others passengers were rescued.
1923 : The former lover of OSCAR WILDE, Lord ALFRED
DOUGLAS, was sentenced to six months's imprisonment for libelling WINSTON CHURCHILL.
1937 : The Japanese Army occupied Nanking.
1952 : A Geelong school teacher came close to breaking
the four minute mile at Olympic Park in Melbourne. JOHN LANDY was only 0.8 of a second outside the seven-year-old world record and shattered the existing Australian record by 4.9 seconds.
1967 : King CONSTANCE of Greece fleed his country after
an unsuccessful attempt to topple the Greek military junta.
1989 : In South Africa, ANC leader NELSON MANDELA met
President F.W. DE KLERK for the first time.
1989 : The first Vietnamese refugees were repatriated
from Hong Kong, escorted to a plane at dawn by police in riot gear.
